record.question: What does the “https://” part of a URL indicate?
options: The protocol used to transfer data
record.explanation: A is uniquely best. The https scheme identifies secure HTTP communication, whereas a URL's authority identifies the server and its path identifies the resource. RFC 9110 defines the https URI scheme for secured HTTP communication. Strictly, https is the scheme name and :// is syntax introducing the authority; saying that this URL part indicates the transfer protocol is a valid introductory interpretation. That syntax precision does not support the server-address, file-location, or search-engine distractors. Precision note: Strictly, https is the URI scheme, and :// introduces the authority. It indicates secure HTTP; this is distinct from the hostname and resource path. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-4.2.2
